rules.pass: The relay listens on its configured P2P address and port.
rules.warn: The relay listens on its P2P port, but on another address than the one configured.
rules.fail: The relay runs and nothing listens on its P2P port.
rules.unknown: The configuration or the socket table could not be read.
rules.skipped: The relay does not run on this host.

advice.listening: The relay listens on its P2P port {port}.
advice.other-address: The relay listens on port {port}, but not on the configured address. Check the P2P host setting, then restart the relay. More: https://docs.iceroot.com/validators/doctor/#net-p2p-listen
advice.not-listening: The relay runs but does not listen on port {port}. Read its log for a bind error. More: https://docs.iceroot.com/validators/doctor/#net-p2p-listen

rules.pass: The API listens on loopback only, is switched off, or no forger uses this relay. Under the onboarding profile a public API is reported as a fact.
rules.warn: The API listens on a non-loopback address on a relay a forger uses.
rules.unknown: The configuration, the socket table or the forger's configuration could not be read.
rules.skipped: The relay does not run on this host.

advice.loopback: The node API listens on loopback only (port {port}).
advice.api-off: The node API is switched off.
advice.no-forger: The node API listens on a public address, but no forger uses this relay.
advice.exposed-onboarding: The node API listens on a public address (port {port}). The application check needs that. A sentry relay is the better place for it; if you opened this port for the check, close it again afterwards.
advice.exposed: The node API listens on a public address on a validator's relay. Public APIs belong on separate API nodes. Set CORE_API_HOST=127.0.0.1, or block port {port} in your firewall. More: https://docs.iceroot.com/validators/hardening/

checks.title: The forger listens on no port

rules.pass: The forger listens on no port.
rules.fail: The forger listens on a port, in any mode.
rules.unknown: The socket table could not be read.
rules.skipped: The forger does not run on this host.

advice.none: The forger listens on no port.
advice.listens: The forger listens on port {port}. It should open none. Report this: it is a defect. More: https://docs.iceroot.com/validators/doctor/#net-forger-no-listener

rules.pass: Every remoteAccess entry is a plain IP address, and the address a forger connects from is listed. With no forger, an empty list is fine.
rules.warn: An entry is not a plain address (a prefix such as 10.0.0.0/24, or a host name), which the relay matches against nothing; or a public address is listed.
rules.fail: The list is empty, or no entry matches the forger's address, while a forger is configured to use this relay.
rules.unknown: The configuration or the forger's configuration could not be read.
rules.skipped: The relay does not run on this host.

advice.listed: The remoteAccess list holds plain addresses only, and the forger's address is among them.
advice.none-needed: The remoteAccess list is empty, and no forger uses this relay.
advice.unmatched-entry: {entries} remoteAccess entries match no address: this relay compares exact addresses only, so a prefix such as 10.0.0.0/24 or a host name admits nobody. List the forger's address itself. More: https://docs.iceroot.com/validators/doctor/#net-remote-access
advice.public-address: A public address is listed in remoteAccess. Only your own forger's address belongs there. More: https://docs.iceroot.com/validators/doctor/#net-remote-access
advice.empty: remoteAccess is empty, so the relay refuses its forger's calls. Add the forger's address (127.0.0.1 when it runs on this host). More: https://docs.iceroot.com/validators/doctor/#net-remote-access
advice.no-match: remoteAccess admits no forger, so the relay refuses its forger's calls. Add the forger's address itself (127.0.0.1 when it runs on this host); prefixes and host names match nothing. More: https://docs.iceroot.com/validators/doctor/#net-remote-access

rules.pass: A host firewall service is active (ufw, nftables or firewalld).
rules.warn: No host firewall service is active. A provider's firewall may stand in, which the doctor cannot see.
rules.unknown: The service states could not be read.

advice.active: A host firewall service is active (ufw {ufw}, nftables {nftables}, firewalld {firewalld}).
advice.none-active: No host firewall service is active (ufw {ufw}, nftables {nftables}, firewalld {firewalld}). If your provider's firewall protects this host, you can ignore this. Otherwise follow the hardening guide's rules: https://docs.iceroot.com/validators/hardening/

rules.unknown: Nothing on this host can prove the relay is reachable from outside, so the finding is always unknown, with advice for testing it.
rules.skipped: The relay does not run on this host.

advice.unverifiable: The doctor cannot see this host from outside. Test the P2P port from a machine that holds no connection to this relay (not your forger's host, not one of your other relays or sentries), for example nc -vz <public address> {port}. A new connection from an address closes that address's other connections to the relay, and a probe that never completes the handshake gets its address banned for about 10 seconds, so a test from the forger's address would cut the forger off.
